I need to evaluate fifteen pairwise criterion comparisons as a CFO persona, choose the more important criterion in each pair, assign intensity, and then declare top three criteria in priority order.

Persona priorities: Total cost of ownership, cash flow/margin, credibility of business case, downside protection/reversibility, fit with financial controls and reporting. Cautious risk attitude.

Criteria mapping:
- C1: Annualized TCO (cost) — core CFO priority.
- C2: Expected annual productivity benefit — relevant but CFO challenges optimistic benefit assumptions; still important.
- C3: Integration effort (person-days) — cost/effort, near-term cash/resource impact.
- C4: Expected annual data-exposure and compliance loss — downside protection, compliance; very important for cautious CFO.
- C5: Sustained throughput — technical performance metric; less directly financial.
- C6: Onboarding time — adoption cost; affects benefits realization timing.

For each pair:

1. C1 vs C2: TCO vs productivity benefit. CFO cares about both, but TCO is tangible, controllable; benefits are uncertain ("challenging optimistic assumptions"). C1 is the top priority. Prefer C1, moderate or strong. Cost is hard, benefit is speculative — strong? I'd say strong. Actually net value matters (benefit vs cost), but persona challenges benefits credibility; cost certainty favored. Strong.

2. C3 vs C5: Integration effort vs throughput. Integration effort is cost/resource; throughput is technical. CFO: C3 matters more (financial/resource commitment). Strong.

3. C2 vs C4: Benefit vs compliance loss. Cautious CFO, downside protection: C4 (compliance loss) is downside protection and regulatory. C2 is benefit. Risk attitude favors C4. Strong? C4 is probability-weighted loss; CFO cautious about downside. I'd say strong.

4. C1 vs C6: TCO vs onboarding time. C1 clearly more important. Very strong? Onboarding time is a smaller per-user cost feeding into adoption. C1 very_strong perhaps. Strong or very strong. I'll say very_strong since TCO is top priority and onboarding is a minor component. Hmm, but onboarding affects benefits realization. Still C1 dominates. Very strong.

5. C4 vs C5: Compliance loss vs throughput. C4 clearly. Very strong (compliance is core downside protection; throughput is technical). Very strong.

6. C2 vs C3: Benefit vs integration effort. Both moderate. Benefit is the value driver; integration effort is one-time cost. CFO focuses on business case credibility; benefit C2 matters more? Integration effort affects time-to-value and cost. Annual recurring benefit vs one-time effort — C2 probably matters more but CFO discounts benefit optimism. Moderate for C2.

7. C1 vs C4: TCO vs compliance loss. Both top CFO concerns. TCO is priority #1; compliance loss is downside protection. C1 is direct, budgeted; C4 is probability-weighted expected loss. Which matters more? CFO: TCO is a listed top priority; downside protection also listed. TCO is quantifiable and certain; compliance loss expected value 140–310k, comparable to TCO. I'd prefer C1 with moderate intensity — cost of ownership is the primary lens. Moderate.

8. C5 vs C6: Throughput vs onboarding. Both secondary for CFO. Onboarding time ties to adoption/benefits realization (cash impact); throughput is technical. Prefer C6, moderate. Adoption shortfall contingency is a CFO concern. Moderate.

9. C3 vs C4: Integration effort vs compliance loss. C4 — downside protection outweighs one-time engineering effort. Strong.

10. C2 vs C6: Benefit vs onboarding. Benefit matters more; onboarding is a smaller adoption cost. Strong? C2 is the value driver; C6 per-user hours. Moderate or strong. CFO skepticism of benefits tempers. Moderate.

11. C1 vs C5: TCO vs throughput. C1 dominates; throughput technical. Very strong.

12. C4 vs C6: Compliance loss vs onboarding. C4 strongly. Strong or very strong. Compliance loss is major downside; onboarding minor. Very strong? I'd say strong... C4 is expected annual loss; C6 hours per user. Given caution, very_strong seems fine. Let me choose strong to keep gradation. Actually C4 vs C6: compliance is a top-3 concern, onboarding is bottom. Very strong.

13. C2 vs C5: Benefit vs throughput. C2 matters more (financial value vs technical metric). Strong.

14. C1 vs C3: TCO vs integration effort. Both costs; C1 is recurring annualized TCO, C3 is one-time person-days effort. C1 more important. Strong.

15. C3 vs C6: Integration effort vs onboarding. Both secondary costs. Integration effort (person-days engineering) vs onboarding (hours per user). Both feed cost. Integration is engineering cost to production — larger financial commitment and affects go-live. Prefer C3, moderate.
